questions.q: What does each numbered .json file inside _delta_log/ represent?
options: One commit — one atomic change made to the table
A single row of data in the table
A backup copy of the entire table
A user permission grant
questions.explain: Opening one shows a sequence of JSON records, each describing one action taken during that write.

questions.q: What does an "add" action in a commit mean?
options: This specific Parquet file is now part of the table
A new column has been added to the table's schema
A new user has been granted access to the table
The table has been renamed
questions.explain: A "remove" action means the opposite — that file is no longer part of the table's current version.

questions.q: When a "remove" action appears in the log, does the underlying Parquet file usually get deleted from disk immediately?
options: No — the file is just marked as no longer current; it usually still exists on disk
Yes, it's deleted from disk the instant the remove action is written
Only if VACUUM has never been run before
The file is immediately moved to a separate archive folder
questions.explain: This is exactly what makes time travel (Lesson 21) possible — old files often still exist physically.

questions.q: What is a checkpoint in the Delta transaction log?
options: A periodic Parquet file summarizing the entire table state, so a reader doesn't have to replay every commit from the beginning
A manual save point a user must trigger before every write
A backup that must be restored before reading the table
A required step before running VACUUM
questions.explain: This is purely an internal optimization — it doesn't change how you read or write a Delta table.

questions.q: How does Spark reconstruct "the current table" when reading a Delta table?
options: Starting from the latest checkpoint, it replays every commit after it, arriving at the set of files with an add never followed by a remove
It always reads every single Parquet file ever written to the table's folder, regardless of add/remove status
It asks a separate metadata database unrelated to _delta_log/
It picks the single most recently modified file in the folder
questions.explain: This is the entire mechanism behind Delta's guarantee that there's no ambiguity about the real current version.
